manual.label: Credit or debit a wallet by hand
manual.help: When on, a team member with the "wallet" permission can add credit to a customer's wallet or take it off by hand, always with a reason and a note (a goodwill credit, a correction the customer agreed to). Every entry is a new line in the wallet's ledger and in the audit log; nothing is ever edited or deleted, and a mistake is put right with a new entry the other way. "Largest entry": the most one entry may be (empty = no limit). A debit never takes a wallet below zero. Off: nobody can change a wallet by hand.

apology.label: Late-delivery apology credit
apology.help: Whether a customer whose parcel came late may get an apology credit in his wallet. "Per order": a team member gives it on the order and types the amount (up to the limit). "By rule": the amount follows from your rule — a fixed amount, or a percentage of the order's goods — and it can only be given once the order came this many hours later than its promise. One credit per order. "Most per order": the limit (empty = no limit). The credit is store credit in the wallet; nothing is paid out and no price changes. Off: no apology credit is given.

refunds.label: Refund rules
refunds.help: When a refund may be asked and how the money goes back. Every refund waits for someone with the "approve refunds" permission (you); the shop never sends money back by itself — after approval a team member sends it the way it came (bKash, bank) and records the reference, or it goes to the customer's wallet as store credit. "Refund to the wallet" (off): real money may go back to the wallet instead. "After delivery" (off): no refunds once the customer received the goods (exchange is the way), except the sources in the list (the rider's overcharge). "Returned prepaid parcel": give everything back, or keep the delivery charge. "Four eyes" (off): the person who asked a refund may not approve it.

partial.label: Partial payment and the pre-order advance
partial.help: Whether a pre-order may be paid partly now and the rest at the door. A team member asks the advance on the order and the customer pays it online (bKash, Nagad, card); only money that came in lowers what the rider collects. "Cap": the most the shop may ask as an advance, as a percentage of the order's total (10% to start). "Smallest advance": below this no payment is asked (empty = no minimum). "Pay it all now" (off): the customer may pay the whole order in advance instead. Off: no advance is asked for a pre-order.

statement.label: Reading the payment services' statements
statement.help: How the statement file of a payment service (bKash, Nagad, card) is read: the column names it may have (the transaction ID, the amount, the fee, the date, the type) and the words that mark a line as money going back (refund, reversal). Every line is matched with our own payment by its transaction ID. "Difference allowed": how many paisa of difference still count as a match (0 = exact). "Missing after": after how many days a paid online payment that no statement shows is listed as missing (0 = off). Nothing is changed and nobody is messaged: a mismatch is only listed, with its reason, for you to check.

reasons.label: Payment statement mismatch reasons
reasons.help: The words for each reason a line of a payment service's statement does not match our records. The reasons themselves are fixed (so reports can count them); only their words are yours. A mismatch is never shown without its reason.

statement.UNKNOWN_PAYMENT: The statement shows money we have no payment for
statement.AMOUNT_DIFFERS: The statement shows another amount than our payment
statement.DOUBLE_LINE: The same payment is on the statement again
statement.NOT_PAID: The statement shows money for a payment we did not record as paid
statement.UNKNOWN_REFUND: The statement shows money sent back that we have no refund for
statement.REFUND_DIFFERS: The statement shows another refund amount than ours
statement.MISSING: A paid online payment is on no statement yet
